outcome_impact: DB password for benchmark@localhost appeared once in agent tool-output transcript; not propagated to any report, file, or commit
what_went_wrong: While diagnosing a hung prep script, I re-ran it with 'bash -x'. The script contains mysql -p"$(cat benchmark_pw)"; bash -x echoes the expanded command line, printing the DB password into the transcript.
root_cause: Using shell tracing (bash -x) on a script that materializes a secret into a process command line. Tracing expands and echoes all substitutions.
contributing: Earlier PowerShell quoting failures pushed me toward -x for visibility instead of narrowing the trace to non-secret lines.
actual_damage: Single exposure in this session transcript (agent + operator visibility). DB is localhost-only; box accessed via SSH. Password not written to any artifact.
remediation_done: Password excluded from final report; no further -x use on secret-bearing scripts; verified no stray benchmark_pw files exist on VPS.
remediation_recommended: Orchestrator may rotate: write new password to /opt/simrs-khanza/run-env/benchmark_pw then 'mysql -uroot -e "ALTER USER benchmark@localhost IDENTIFIED BY \"<new>\""' and re-run PatchDbXml for run-env/setting/database.xml (credentials are AES-embedded there).
rule_references: brief constraint: do not print DB password
